### 1. Scene
A plate of overlapping flatbread triangles, a small amount of pale sliced meat or topping, cucumber, and roasted yellow vegetables. The dim lighting makes the topping and vegetable type uncertain.

### 2. Vessel
Likely a **26 cm dinner plate**, partly cropped at the top.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### 3–7. Items, coverage, volume, weight, and energy
Coverage is allocated without double-counting overlapping items. The roasted vegetables appear lightly oily; their energy estimate includes that oil rather than adding it separately.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × typical height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Flatbread triangles | 32% | 170 cm² × 0.85 cm = 145 ml | 0.95 | 138 g | 280 | 386 kcal |
| Pale sliced meat/topping, probably chicken | 6% | 32 cm² × 0.9 cm = 29 ml | 1.0 | 29 g | 165 | 48 kcal |
| Cucumber pieces | 10% | 53 cm² × 1.3 cm = 69 ml | 0.6 | 41 g | 15 | 6 kcal |
| Roasted yellow vegetables, likely squash, with light oil | 18% | 96 cm² × 2 cm = 192 ml | 0.6 | 115 g | 100 | 115 kcal |

### 8. Sanity check
Allocated coverage totals **66% of the plate**, consistent with the visible bare rim and right side. The estimated **323 g and 555 kcal** are plausible for a modest pile of flatbread with vegetables and a small topping. Identification and bread thickness are the largest uncertainties.
